pr_title: Send null for invalidate on flush
pr_body:
Fixes #7463 
When a flush occurs, redis intends to send clients with tracking enabled an empty string to indicate that all keys are invalid. Before, the code contains a bug that sends a bulk string of length 1 when it means to use 0.

Regardless, there is no safe bulk string to use for a special value for "invalidate all" because any bulk string potentially conflicts with a valid Redis key.

Instead, send a RESP NULL to indicate flush.
pr_comments: @madolson @lukepalmer I still believe the last filed `proto` should depend on the client is tracking in `BCAST` mode or not. Since `BCAST` client expects an array, but other client need only one key.

Thank you for the detail, I'll take a look at this.

I'm less familiar with BCAST mode so I'll have to do some digging. @soloestoy, if you believe you know what needs to be done, tips very much appreciated.

@soloestoy I think in all cases the clients are expecting a list of keys based on the implementation, which I think is correct since we want the same protocol. The BCAST mode will send a list of N keys that have been modified and the TRACKING mode will send a list of a single key. So I guess we have a couple of options on flush:
1. The current implementation is instead of sending a list, we send null. I think this makes sense still. 
2. We can tweak the current implementation where we send a list with a single null item. I was originally thinking this, but I think 1 makes more sense.
3. Send some other message, which seems worse from a client side since they have to do a type check to figure out what they are supposed to do about it. 

I think the documentation should probably be clarified a bit though, looking at the surrounding code it seems like some of the comments are no longer correct.

>1. The current implementation is instead of sending a list, we send null. I think this makes sense still.

OK, I agree with that. Sending a list of a single null is a bit odd, sending null is more appropriate.

Thanks @madolson @lukepalmer , just approved this PR.

Hello @soloestoy @madolson, I have another question regarding the trackingInvalidateKeysOnFlush function, maybe not related to this pr, but I think it may save time to ask here: we passed in the dbid parameter to this function, if we did flushall(dbid == -1), we clean up the tracking table, however, for both cases, we did flushdb or flushall, we all send (null) to all clients in order to instruct clients to clean up all client-side cache. so what was the reason we still keep tracking table for normal flushdb case? thanks!

issue_context.title: Client tracking pushes null invalidate upon flush
issue_context.body:
Flushing a Redis appears to create an "invalidate" message containing a null byte. 
Is this intentional? If so, it's undocumented.

Reproduction, using RESP3:
```
client tracking on
flushall

```
Message received is:
`>2\r\n$10\r\ninvalidate\r\n*1\r\n$1\r\n\0\r\n`

It would be great to document RESP3 push messages in general, especially invalidate.
comments: It is intended behavior. On flushing all, or most of, the data we don't want to send invalidation messages for every key you might have tracked (That would be very expensive) so we send a single NULL message instead. I agree about the missing documentation. Might be better to create a request over in the documentation repo: https://github.com/redis-io/redis-doc

One problem.

>This is good, because a null byte is a valid redis key that would otherwise be indistinguishable from the "invalidate everything" message.

User can use NULL key name, just like `SET "" v`, I'm not sure if some users do that, but it's valid. So if we send NULL message, it may be confused if it is `FLUSHALL` or a real key name?

Long before that, when we use slot to tracking, we user `-1` to represent `FLUSHALL`, but now maybe we need a new channel.

@soloestoy 
One possible fix is to send an actual "NULL" back, which has its own special character in RESPV2 and RESPV3. I think it's $-1/r/n and _\n. We should figure out if we think we'l need more special characters. Having to listen to multiple channels sounds like it will overly complicate client implementations.
@madolson I like that, it's simpler than what I thought of first. Happy to implement if people are on board.
@lukepalmer Sounds like that is probably the best fix for now, so I think you can go and implement it if you want.

I implemented null on invalidate and updated the pull request. 

I'd love to get this merged if everyone likes this.

review_comments: Here I think the proto should depend on client's flags is `BCAST` or not.

This will need to be at a lower level. Right now you're just passing binary representation of a null as the keyname (e.g. "-1\r\n"), which is a valid. You'll need to call addReply(shared.null[c->resp]) directly somewhere, probably in sendTrackingMessage() if the keyname is NULL.

Thank you for looking @madolson!

Could you help me understand a bit more about what I've gotten wrong here? Based on the function docs I would have expected that when specifying the 4th argument of this function as '1' that a preformatted message would be allowed in the 2nd argument. If that's not right and you can tell me a bit more, then I could also update function docs for sendTrackingMessage.
My bad, I missed that you updated that the last field. So I think this change looks good.
